title: Chat envelope marshaler: map OpenAI ChatCompletions request/response to Redwood v2 streaming & function model
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Provide a compatibility marshaler that translates OpenAI ChatCompletions (requests and streaming responses) into Redwood's canonical v2 streaming and function/tool calling model. Goal: allow legacy clients and partners that expect OpenAI semantics to use Redwood endpoints without behavioral regressions while enabling Redwood-native telemetry and graceful fallbacks. This ticket covers the mapping rules, edge cases for streaming function arguments, error-code mapping, and a canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Requests using OpenAI ChatCompletions JSON schema are accepted and produce equivalent Redwood inference behavior for non-functional and functional flows
Streamed deltas from models are translated into Redwood chunk events without dropping role/name metadata and preserve partial function_call arguments until complete
Tool/function calls emitted by models arrive as Redwood tool.invoke/tool.result events with preserved provenance and idempotency keys
OpenAI-style error responses (including rate limit 429, context_length_exceeded) are mapped to Redwood error envelopes and surfaced to clients with consistent retry hints
Automated test harness verifies 20+ synthetic conversation permutations including nested function calls, truncated argument streams, and mixing of structured output tokens
Canary shows <0.5% malformed-tool-call rate before full rollout
implementation_notes: Input mapping: map OpenAI messages[] -> Redwood.messages with fields {role, name, content} and keep user-supplied metadata in message.metadata.redwood_compat

Streaming: convert OpenAI SSE/chunked 'delta' pieces into Redwood streaming frames. Each frame should include 'token', 'role' iff present in the delta, and 'partial_function_args' when function_call.arguments are streaming.

Function calling: OpenAI sometimes streams function_call.arguments as a sequence of text chunks. Buffer until a complete JSON object is received (heuristic: balanced braces + valid JSON) then emit a single tool.invoke with arguments. If stream ends with malformed JSON, emit tool.invoke with raw_text and mark 'parse_error' in metadata.
Idempotency: attach an idempotency key derived from OpenAI's request id or generated per-request. Use for dedup across retries and for matching partial streams to final completion events.
Backpressure: support pausing upstream model stream consumption when downstream clients are congested. Emit a 'stall' telemetry event if buffering exceeds 4MB or 5s latency.

Telemetry: map OpenAI finish_reason -> Redwood outcome codes and emit token-level latency and per-frame network timings. Add metrics: compat.malformed_frames, compat.function_call_parse_errors, compat.stream_restarts
Error mapping: map OpenAI HTTP 429 -> Redwood RATE_LIMIT with suggested_retry_after (ms); 400 -> BAD_REQUEST with cause; 413 -> CONTEXT_LENGTH_EXCEEDED

Security: do not forward OpenAI-specific internal headers. Remove X-OpenAI-* provenance headers unless explicitly allowed by customer config. Record redaction events in audit logs for Private deployments.
checklist: Design review with API and SDK teams
Unit tests for message mapping and streaming arithmetic
Integration tests against a legacy OpenAI consumer simulator
End-to-end canary deployment (5% traffic) with automated rollback
Docs: compatibility guide + migration notes for partners
Docs: example code snippets for Node/Python clients

2025-02-12 Liam Chen: Spike completed. Found two common streaming patterns: (1) role token emitted as its own delta, (2) function_call.arguments arriving as a raw text stream. Proposed buffering approach in implementation_notes. Created initial PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6271
2025-02-14 Design sync: agreed to preserve message.metadata for downstream SDKs. PM requested explicit compatibility toggle per-API key. Will add feature flagging in runtime config.

2025-02-17 QA note: added fuzz test cases for truncated JSON in function args; current behavior: emit tool.invoke with parse_error metadata and store raw payload for later inspection. Need to confirm visible error shape for legacy clients.

2025-02-19 Liam Chen: Implementation WIP. Marshaler packaged as 'compat/openai_chat_marshaler' and wired behind feature flag. Unit tests for balanced brace heuristic pass; integration tests against simulator show 0.18% malformed-tool-call on first run — investigating edge case in chunk boundary handling.
2025-02-20 Ava Martinez: Updated acceptance criteria to include canary threshold and telemetry metrics. Plan: roll canary 2025-02-25, monitor compat.* metrics for 48h before scaling to 50%.
Follow-ups: add SDK examples for streaming partial function arguments, update console dashboards to surface compat.* events, add RBAC toggle for Private deployments to disable compatibility mapping.
